title: A connected scheme with a rational point is geometrically connected
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $X$ is connected and that there is $s:\operatorname{Spec}(k)\to X$ with $f\circ s=\mathrm{id}$. Then for every field extension $K/k$, $X\times_k K$ is connected.

proof.text: Use the existing, proved GeometricallyConnected.of_connectedSpace_of_section in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Geometrically.Connected (Stacks 04KV). Its proof first proves connectedness after algebraic extension via the open and closed integral projection and the singleton fibre over the rational point. It passes to an algebraic closure, where connected implies geometrically connected, and descends connectedness along the surjective projection from a common algebraically closed extension.
